subject: Night shift SLA split-coverage proposal (temporary)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Sara Hudson <sara.hudson@tritonhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Night shift SLA split-coverage proposal (temporary)

Team,

Triton has reported a cluster of overnight P1/P2 incidents over the past two weeks tied to their nightly ETL jobs. Their CS lead (Sara) and I spoke this morning — they’re asking whether we can provide a short-term change to our on-call response pattern to improve time-to-first-response between 00:00–06:00 PT for the next 6 weeks while they harden jobs.

Proposal (temporary; 6 weeks):
- Split on-call coverage into two overlapping night shifts (00:00–04:00 PT and 03:30–07:30 PT) to ensure an overlap window for handoff and faster warm-start response.
- Maintain P1 escalation 24/7 to engineering manager and on-call lead (no change).
- Adjust P2 first-response target from 30m -> 45m during the 00:00–06:00 window for teams that cannot staff an additional overnight engineer; during overlap windows we target 30m.
- CS to perform first-line triage for P2s originating from scheduled jobs, escalate to on-call if signs of system degradation.

Why: This will reduce mean time-to-detect during the low-visibility window and give Triton faster triage while we finalize fixes. Operational impact: small additional coverage hours for volunteers; calendar templates and rotation logic required.

Requested actions:
- Marcus: quick ops impact estimate (hours/cost) and whether runtime routing needs any config changes.
- Lauren: approval flow and whether leadership sign-off is required for a temporary SLA boundary change.
- Sara: confirm Triton is comfortable with keeping P1 escalation unchanged and if they can accept temporary P2 response window adjustments.

Attachments: SLO matrix and proposed calendar.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Night shift SLA split-coverage proposal (temporary)

Vanessa — thanks for the writeup, makes sense as a pragmatic approach. A couple quick notes: 
- Ops: splitting shifts as proposed adds roughly 1.4 FTE-weeks over 6 weeks if staffed by volunteers; if we backfill with contractors it’s ~USD 9k.
- Runtime: no routing or model-level config changes expected; this is purely staffing/rota + notification template changes.
- Monitoring: we should add a temporary PagerDuty escalation rule that pins the on-call lead during overlap windows.

If we go ahead I can put together the PD rule and update the rotation scripts; will need final approval from Lauren for the SLA exception.

Thanks for the clear proposal. I support a time-boxed exception provided we: 
1) Document the exception and communicate to affected customers (email + status page banner).
2) Create a short-lived Jira (SUP-2217) to track implementation, on-call assignments, and post-mortem metrics.
3) Keep P1 escalation unchanged — P1s must still route to engineering manager and the on-call SRE immediately.
4) Define measurable success: reduce P1/P2 time-to-first-response by 20% in the overnight window or revert to standard rota.

I will: 
- Approve the exception pending Marcus’ exact hours/cost estimate.
- Notify Legal for a quick sign-off (we're not changing contractual SLA text, just operational targets for a pilot).

Please get the timeline and PD rule to me by EOD. I'll loop in Legal and put a short note on my calendar to review metrics after 6 weeks.

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Support Operations
Redwood Inference
